findings.description: The bucket is not configured with server-side encryption, so data stored in it is unencrypted at rest, exposing sensitive data to anyone with access to the underlying storage.
The bucket is explicitly noted as public (no acl set to private and no block_public_access configured), allowing potential public read/write access to data stored inside.
The bucket has no access logging configured, so there is no audit trail of who accesses data within the bucket, hampering detection of unauthorized access.
Versioning is not enabled on the bucket, so accidental deletion or overwriting of objects cannot be recovered, and no history of object versions is retained for security forensics.
The financials bucket is not configured with server-side encryption, leaving sensitive financial data stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no access logging configured, so there is no audit trail of who accesses financial data, hampering detection of unauthorized access.
The operations bucket is not configured with server-side encryption, leaving data stored within it unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has no access logging configured, so there is no audit trail of who accesses operational data, hampering detection of unauthorized access.
The data_science bucket is not configured with server-side encryption, leaving data stored within it unencrypted at rest.
A customer-master.xlsx object (likely containing customer data) is uploaded to a public unencrypted bucket, exposing sensitive customer information to unauthorized access.
